notes: Landlord-tenant window-liability case involving a family's leased apartment; the Philadelphia Housing Code language is quoted only in the dissent as a footnote on 'the trend of the times' and is expressly inapplicable to the facts. No lodging/boarding issue is litigated.
Dispute over holdover tenancy and a rent increase for a store-plus-apartment premises rented to a family under a written lease. Ordinary landlord-tenant rent litigation, not lodging or boarding.
Office-building owner's regulation restricting outside towel-supply vendors from soliciting business among its office tenants. No residential lodging/boarding issue.
Tax-sale notice/terre-tenant dispute among heirs of an inherited residence. No letting or lodging arrangement at issue.

Case decides whether a garage attached to a hotel-apartment building is a nuisance per se. Facts note the hotel's transient guests typically stay overnight, but this is background only; the holding concerns garage construction/nuisance law under the police power, not the legal character or regulation of the lodging itself.

holding_summary: A deed restriction limiting buildings to "private dwelling houses" was violated when the owner added a second kitchen and bathroom to convert the house into a two-family dwelling; the court held "private" excludes multi-family/apartment occupancy and affirmed an injunction confining the property to single-family use.

quotes.text: An apartment house is none the less a dwelling house though occupied by a number of families but it is not a private dwelling house. The term ‘private’ in that connection means limitation for use privately, that is, apart from others, or in other words, singly by one family.

An apartment house is none the less a dwelling house though occupied by a number of families but it is not a private dwelling house. The term ‘private’ in that connection means limitation for use privately, that is, apart from others, or in other words, singly by one family.
The decree is affirmed at appellants’ cost.

notes: Owner altered a single-family house to accommodate two families (added second kitchen/bath); record does not state whether the second unit was rented for pay or occupied by relatives, and does not state a term length, so who_was_letting/duration are conservative.
One-paragraph per curiam affirmance holding the motel/tourist-court zoning appeal moot in light of the companion case Harrisburg v. Pass; no facts or doctrine discussed.

court: Blair County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Dispute between lessor and lessee-operator of the 'Cross Keys Inn' over rent and lease forfeiture following a liquor-law prosecution. Concerns the inn as leased commercial property, not the character of guest lodging.

court: Luzerne County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Determines whether a tenancy-by-the-entirety qualifies its holder as a 'freeholder' exempt from arrest on a capias. Unrelated to lodging or boarding.

court: Philadelphia County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Constructive-service/mortgagee-in-possession dispute arising from a sidewalk injury. No lodging or boarding issue; 'user' of real estate is analyzed for service-of-process purposes only.

court: Washington County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Lease-covenant 'subletting' dispute where a tenant family's son-in-law lived with them for several months after his marriage, without a separate rent payment; court held this was not a subletting. No compensated-occupancy relationship at issue.
Declaratory-judgment action over whether a commercial lessee holding over after a five-year term became a month-to-month tenant absent an exercised renewal option. Not a lodging/boarding case.

court: Philadelphia County Court of Common Pleas
holding_summary: The court held a lease clause exculpating a landlord from liability for injuries caused by defective stairs and lighting in an apartment house is void as against public policy, because it conflicts with the Philadelphia Housing Code's minimum safety standards for rooming/dwelling units, and denied the landlord's motion for judgment on the pleadings.

quotes.text: no person shall . . . let . . . any . . . rooming unit which does not comply with the following minimum standards for light. . . .
an apartment house owned and operated by defendant in which plaintiff was a tenant.
The motion for judgment on the pleadings is dismissed.

notes: Housing-code safety regulation of rooming/dwelling units is sustained as overriding a private exculpatory lease clause; duration of the underlying tenancy is not stated.

court: Philadelphia County Court of Common Pleas
holding_summary: Construing a deed restriction limiting use to "private dwellings or residential purposes," the court held the disjunctive phrasing permits construction of an 11-unit apartment house, distinguishing precedent that bars apartment use under restrictions confined strictly to "private dwelling house."

quotes.text: We are convinced that an apartment house use is permitted within the language "residential purposes".
We are convinced that an apartment house use is permitted within the language "residential purposes".
it is ordered and decreed that plaintiffs’ complaint be and the same is dismissed, all parties to pay their own costs

notes: Multi-unit apartment development permitted as a 'residential purpose'; case does not address occupancy duration or specific lease/license terms for individual units.

The zoning ordinance already permitted apartment houses as a special exception in the district; the appeal turns solely on whether the site plan's setback dimensions comply with the ordinance. No discussion of occupancy character or the letting/lodging doctrine.

Per curiam affirmance of a zoning variance converting a property previously used under a 1940 variance for 'two housekeeping units and seven rooming units' into six apartment units; review is limited to abuse-of-discretion/error-of-law, with no substantive discussion of the character of rooming vs. apartment occupancy. The prior rooming-unit fact may be of interest to the Planner but the holding itself does not engage the doctrine.
Orphans' court partition proceeding surcharging a cotenant heir for the rental value of his exclusive possession of the family home. Not a letting/lodging arrangement with an outside party.
Workers' compensation case defining 'premises of the employer' for an employee crossing a sidewalk 'reservation' strip to reach her workplace. No lodging or boarding issue.
